Why this page exists

A note to Max

"There isn't an open role that fits, so I built this instead." ElevenLabs Canada launched in July with plans to double a 13-person team by year end and open a Toronto office.

Max,

Congratulations on the GM role. Taking a team spread across Toronto, Montréal and Vancouver and turning it into a real Canadian business in a single year is the hardest version of the job. The playbook doesn't exist yet, the first enterprise logos become the reference story for everything after, and every hire compounds.

I want to be the senior enterprise seller on your team who also helps you build the bench. I've done both. As a strategic account executive I carried some of Canada's most complex retail and consumer accounts, and as a Director I led a 10-person enterprise team across six offices.

I'm not asking for a title. I'm asking for 20 minutes to see whether the build you're running could use this.

Chris

The proposal

Player-coach, not overhead

Four jobs I'd take off your plate, in the order they matter for a founding team.

01

Carry the strategic book

Own a focused set of Canada's largest enterprises from first meeting to production deployment: multi-year account strategy, multithreading across business units, and C-suite sponsorship. It's the work I did across Canadian retail and consumer goods, closing roughly $10M in strategic TCV as a strategic AE.

02

Write the enterprise playbook

Turn early wins into something repeatable: ideal customer profile, use-case library, qualification, mutual action plans and reference stories. I was the sole field seller who co-built Salesforce's first global account-based go-to-market model for Healthcare & Life Sciences, later adopted across its global sales organization.

03

Hire and coach the bench

Help you interview, onboard and ramp AEs and SDRs as the team doubles. More than five years of people leadership: 3.5 years of first-line management with full P&L at Enterprise Rent-A-Car, then a 10-person enterprise team across six offices at Salesforce, delivering 30%+ of the vertical's revenue.

04

Deploy with partners, not just sign

Voice agents only create value in production. On virtually every deal I sold, I oversaw the systems integrator through rollout, stayed on adoption with Salesforce's Premier and Signature Success teams, and co-sourced new business with those partners at Loblaw, The Beer Store and Walmart.

Day one, I carry a number.

This isn't a pitch for a management layer. It's a senior seller who has already built a playbook from scratch and already led a team, available when you need both.

Point of view

Where voice agents win in Canada

What I'd bring to the account strategy on day one, grounded in how Canadian enterprises actually buy.

MARKET

Canada is a concentrated enterprise market

A small number of banks, telcos, insurers, grocers and retailers run most of the country's large customer operations. That rewards named-account strategy and multithreading across business units, not volume. Your founding SDR posting already describes exactly this motion; a senior seller who has worked those buying committees makes it land faster.

LANGUAGE & TRUST

Bilingual and privacy-reviewed is table stakes

Quebec customers expect French-first service, and Quebec's Law 25 adds privacy obligations on top of PIPEDA, so voice deployments get scrutinized early. I've closed net-new work in Quebec, including one of Canada's first CDP deals with Harnois Énergies and a Data Cloud and Marketing Cloud win across Groupe CH and the Montréal Canadiens.

ARCHITECTURE

Agents are only as good as the context beneath them

ElevenAgents read and update CRM records mid-conversation. In Salesforce's published Agentic Enterprise reference architecture, voice agents sit in the Agency and Engagement layers, and they win or lose on the layers underneath. Those are the layers I sold for twelve years.

EngagementVoice as the interface
AgencyElevenAgents
WorkWorkflows, CRM, contact centre
ContextCustomer data, identity, consent
ECOSYSTEM

Many of Canada's largest enterprises run Salesforce

ElevenLabs integrates natively with Salesforce, and Salesforce Ventures is an investor. I know that ecosystem from the inside: how its buyers evaluate, how their admins and data teams decide what an agent may touch, and how the systems integrators deploy. Add the federal goal of lifting business AI adoption from 12% to 60% by 2034, and the timing is right.

First 90 days

Learn, open, prove

A player-coach plan: selling from week one, building the system as we go.

Days 1–30
Learn and map
  • Build my own agent on ElevenAgents and own the demo cold.
  • Map the top Canadian enterprise accounts with you: CX stack, CRM, contact-centre platform, likely sponsor.
  • Join every live enterprise deal; take the ones you want me to run.
Days 31–60
Open and qualify
  • Open strategic pursuits in the named book alongside the SDR engine.
  • Draft the Canada enterprise playbook: ICP, use cases, qualification, mutual action plans, French-language requirements.
  • Map the systems integrators and ecosystem partners who will deploy with us.
Days 61–90
Prove and scale
  • Move first pursuits into scoped pilots with agreed success metrics.
  • Turn the first win into a reference story the whole team can sell.
  • Help you interview and onboard the next AEs, and set a weekly pipeline and forecast rhythm the team inherits.

How I lead

Coach first, evidence always

Servant leadership

My job as a leader is to remove blockers, coach in the deal rather than about it, and align the team around evidence rather than opinion. In a founding team that means rolling up my sleeves on the hardest pursuits and making sure every win teaches the next hire something.

Built from zero, twice

I co-founded Salesforce's national employee network for Black professionals in Canada and grew it from zero to 500+ members. Today I serve as Board Secretary and Strategy Lead at BLKOWNED, building partnerships with McMaster DeGroote and Sheridan College.
